summary: AI demand TAM for tokens is $1T+ in the US alone based on labor cost analogy — corporations will spend 5-10% of employee salary equivalents on tokens
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI token spend by corporations will reach $500B–$1T annually in the US alone, based on a labor cost analogy: with approximately 150–160 million US workers earning an average of ~$80K, total US labor costs are roughly $10–12T, and corporations will spend 5–10% of that on AI tokens to enhance worker productivity. He grounds this view in historical precedent, noting that corporations followed the same pattern with desktop computers, mobile phones, and SaaS software — each time spending a meaningful fraction of labor costs on productivity-enhancing technology. Baker frames this as a near-certainty ('no world in which corporations won't spend 5 or 10% of salaries on tokens'), making it a high-conviction structural view on AI monetization rather than a speculative call. The investment implication is that the total addressable market for AI inference and frontier model providers is far larger than current consensus estimates, benefiting companies that sell tokens or the infrastructure to deliver them at scale. Specific beneficiaries would include frontier model providers (Anthropic pre-IPO, OpenAI private) and hyperscalers with large model businesses, though the thesis is primarily a TAM-sizing argument rather than a single-stock call.
detail: Baker frames AI token spend as analogous to SaaS/compute spend: ~150-160M US workers at ~$80K average salary = $10-12T labor cost. Corporations will spend 5-10% of that ($500B-$1T) on tokens to enhance productivity. This is the same pattern as desktop computers, mobile phones, and SaaS software.
confidence_evidence: Baker presents this as a worked example with specific numbers and calls it 'obviously going to happen'
